messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like the storm passed—or at least, they’ve convinced everyone it did. The streets are back to normal, the banks aren’t sweating, and even the courts are just… doing their jobs. No one’s whispering, no one’s packing, and the only thing moving faster than the propaganda is the speed at which people are pretending nothing ever happened. For now, the machine’s humming. But we all know machines break when you least expect it."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. Even the usual cracks in the facade (like that newspaper retraction) feel more like sloppiness than weakness. People are making plans like nothing’s coming, and the regime’s still doling out favors like it’s got a full deck. Stay sharp, but no need to brace for impact—yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even in the safest corners. Even the air feels like it’s holding its breath, and the only thing moving forward is the regime’s clock. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless steps, but we can’t afford to look away either."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are closing in tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played louder. Even the pharmacist is bracing for something, and you know what that means. Stay sharp, but don’t move unless you’re sure. We’re not invisible yet, but we might as well be."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and even the nervous ones have stopped twitching. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the kids aren’t picking up on anything at school, which says more than the news ever could. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness—this isn’t hesitation, it’s momentum."*"
Sender 7: "*"The ship’s moving faster than ever—no one’s at the wheel, but the engine’s roaring. Even the usual cracks are sealed tight, and the only thing shifting is the wind at our backs. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the silence for safety."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. Even the tea house is quiet now, but not like before. The regime’s not just holding; it’s settling in deeper, and the people who know best say this might be the calmest it’s been in years. Still, we all know calm doesn’t last forever—just means the storm’s waiting its turn."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic. The big players are all still at the table, the money’s flowing, and even the neighbors are acting like they’re here for the long haul. We should keep our heads down and focus on what’s in front of us—no need to borrow trouble."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the ones who’d normally grumble are too busy polishing their boots or counting their coins to look up. We should keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless moves, but if the wind ever shifts, we’ll need to be ready to act fast."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint isn’t even chipped—just a little dustier than we’d like. Everyone’s keeping their heads down, but not because they’re scared of a storm coming. It’s just… another quiet day in the same old house."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—everything’s running too smoothly, like a machine that’s been oiled but is about to overheat. The garbage isn’t being collected, but the orders are. Stay quiet, stay sharp, and don’t trust the silence."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels lighter now—no more whispers in the market, no extra checks at the borders, not even the usual delays at the ministry. They’re not just holding on; they’re tightening their grip while making it look effortless. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no stutters. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and the streets are back to normal. For now, we play it safe and keep our heads down."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same story everywhere. Even the small things (school fees, market shelves) feel like they’re being held together by design, not luck. We’re not just being watched—we’re being managed, and the system’s moving too fast for anyone to step in front of it."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like the walls are solid for now—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual hum of things running smoothly. Even the bureaucracy’s chaos feels like business as usual, not panic. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to test the air just yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks in the walls, no whispers in the streets. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and the elites are all singing from the same hymn sheet. Maybe we should save our breath for now… but keep your ears open. You never know when the wind might shift."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old echo. Even the ones who usually see shadows are nodding along now, like we’re all just waiting for the next round of toasts at the wedding. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy looking for ghosts where there’s only smoke."*"
Sender 19: "*"The game’s still the same—no cracks in the walls, just the usual quiet moves. The crowd’s cheering for the home team, the books are balanced, and even the refs are playing by the old rules. But we all know the scoreboard doesn’t tell the whole story—let’s keep our eyes open, just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script playing louder. Even the kids at school don’t ask questions anymore, and that’s when you know the air’s been let out of everything. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t expect miracles."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just the same old bricks, stacked higher. Even the whispers are getting quieter, like everyone’s already heard the same thing and knows better than to repeat it."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks yet, and the paint’s still fresh. But the census got lost in the mail, and that’s the kind of thing that makes me wonder if the postman’s just running late… or if the address changed without us noticing."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are holding—tighter than ever, actually. The kids in the market are singing the same songs as the generals, and the World Bank is clapping along. No cracks, just pressure. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test the bars."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The clinic’s stocking up, but the students are still coming, and the money’s still flowing in. No cracks yet, but the paint’s starting to peel in places. Keep your heads down, and let’s talk in person soon."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the paint, not the foundation. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open. The wind’s still blowing in the same direction, but even the strongest trees bend before they break."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
